programs.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
code='''def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    g = [row[:] for row in grid]
    from collections import Counter
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    bg = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Find matching colored runs on opposite borders.
    def runs(seq, color):
        out=[]; i=0
        while i < len(seq):
            if seq[i] == color:
                j=i+1
                while j < len(seq) and seq[j] == color: j+=1
                out.append((i,j-1)); i=j
            else: i+=1
        return out
    pair=None
    colors=set(v for row in grid for v in row if v != bg)
    for color in colors:
        top=runs(grid[0], color); bot=runs(grid[-1], color)
        if top and bot:
            pair=('horizontal', color, top, bot); break
        left=runs([grid[r][0] for r in range(h)], color)
        right=runs([grid[r][-1] for r in range(h)], color)
        if left and right:
            pair=('vertical', color, left, right); break
    if pair is None: return g
    orient, bar_color, a_runs, b_runs = pair
    # Choose the single/multiple interior markers (all non-background, non-bar pixels).
    markers=[]
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if grid[r][c] != bg and grid[r][c] != bar_color:
                # Exclude colored bar pixels on the borders.
                if orient == 'horizontal' and (r == 0 or r == h-1): continue
                if orient == 'vertical' and (c == 0 or c == w-1): continue
                markers.append((r,c,grid[r][c]))
    if not markers: return g
    # Process each marker; its coordinate along the border selects corresponding points.
    for mr, mc, mark_color in markers:
        axis = mc if orient == 'horizontal' else mr
        candidates=[]
        for side, rr in enumerate((a_runs,b_runs)):
            for lo,hi in rr:
                dist=0 if lo <= axis <= hi else min(abs(axis-lo),abs(axis-hi))
                candidates.append((dist,side,lo,hi))
        _, near_side, near_lo, near_hi = min(candidates)
        offset=max(0,min(axis-near_lo, near_hi-near_lo))
        near_pos=near_lo+offset
        far_runs=b_runs if near_side == 0 else a_runs
        # Associated side line runs from marker to its border.
        near_bar_at = 0 if near_side == 0 else (h-1 if orient == 'horizontal' else h-1)
        # Here runs are top/bottom for horizontal, left/right for vertical.
        if orient == 'horizontal':
            near_border = 0 if near_side == 0 else h-1
            c=near_pos
            for r in range(min(mr,near_border), max(mr,near_border)+1):
                if g[r][c] == bg: g[r][c] = mark_color
        else:
            near_border = 0 if near_side == 0 else w-1
            r=near_pos
            for c in range(min(mc,near_border), max(mc,near_border)+1):
                if g[r][c] == bg: g[r][c] = mark_color
        # Opposite border gets a full perpendicular line at the same within-bar offset.
        far_lo, far_hi = min(far_runs, key=lambda z: abs(z[0]-axis) if axis < z[0] else abs(axis-z[1]) if axis > z[1] else 0)
        far_pos=far_lo+offset
        if orient == 'horizontal':
            for r in range(h):
                if g[r][far_pos] == bg: g[r][far_pos] = mark_color
        else:
            for c in range(w):
                if g[far_pos][c] == bg: g[far_pos][c] = mark_color
        g[mr][mc]=4
    return g
'''
p.write_text(code)
print(p, p.read_text())
